# Now 2.13.8
- Further lowered full-screen CPU during lyric scrolling. The lyric list now only lays out the lines that are actually on screen instead of the entire song, so each line change is much cheaper to render. Diagnosed from a live CPU profile showing the full lyric list being re-laid-out on every scroll frame.

# Now 2.13.7
- Cut CPU while the full-screen view is open. A live profile showed the progress bar was refreshing 4×/second, and each refresh forced the whole full-screen view (all lyric text included) to re-render. The progress line now updates once a second — standard for a time display — which reduces those full-view re-renders roughly 4×.

# Now 2.13.6
- Major CPU fix. A live CPU profile revealed the app kept running its lyric render loops even for windows that were hidden or covered — the full-screen view's timers kept firing after it was closed, and the desktop overlay kept animating behind the full-screen view. Simply hiding a window (which the previous fix relied on) does not stop those timers. - Now the SwiftUI content is fully torn down when a surface isn't visible: the full-screen view is rebuilt each time it opens and destroyed on close, and the overlay's content is detached whenever it's hidden or covered. Visible, in-use lyrics are unchanged; hidden windows now cost effectively nothing.
